description: The CVEs CISA has added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, newest first, from EchelonGraph's copy of that catalog, which polls CISA's feed every 5 minutes. Each kev row gives cve_id, kev_added_date (CISA's dateAdded), kev_due_date, kev_vendor, kev_product, kev_vuln_name and kev_ransomware (known ransomware-campaign use), EchelonGraph's severity, cvss_v3_score, epss_score, epss_percentile and eg_kev_tier for the CVE, and our_first_seen_kev, when EchelonGraph's poller first recorded the CVE entering the catalog (null where no such record exists). Filter by since and until (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, on kev_added_date), ransomware, and vendor (an exact, case-insensitive match on kev_vendor); page with limit (1 to 200, default 50) and cursor, passing back the previous page's next_cursor with the same filters. total counts the CVEs matching the filters; kev_listed_total counts every CVE EchelonGraph holds as KEV-listed, and catalog.catalog_count is CISA's own count in the catalog last fetched, so a gap between the two is entries not yet in EchelonGraph's CVE table, which no page returns. CISA's requiredAction, shortDescription and notes are not in these rows: each CVE's own record carries them, verbatim and labelled as CISA's. Its structured result's measured_at is our last successful fetch of CISA's feed (null when the API does not say), coverage counts the CISA KEV catalog (total, returned, kev_listed_total, catalog_count, limit, has_more) and freshness gives last_successful_fetch_at, catalog_version and date_released. Past 30,000 characters of JSON, the first text block holds data cut to fit, and the note says what the cut leaves out and where to read it (TEXT CUT); so is structured data (DATA CUT), unless full: true. Cut, each row keeps cve_id, kev_added_date, kev_vendor and kev_ransomware at least, or rows are left out, and next_cursor still continues after the page's last row, not the text's.

full.description: true: data in the structured result is the answer whole, however long. Without it, a structured result past 30,000 characters of JSON has its data cut (DATA CUT): in an order the note states, the entries of its longest lists keep only some of their fields, and then the lists only some of their entries; data_truncated is true, and truncated gives each list cut with its total, the number returned and whether its entries are thinned. Whole data is for a program; a client that sizes structured results, as Claude Code does against MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS, can refuse an answer past its cap.

ransomware.description: true: only CVEs with known ransomware-campaign use; false: only those without

since.description: earliest kev_added_date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (an RFC 3339 timestamp is read as the date written in it, with the time and offset dropped; anything else is refused)

until.description: latest kev_added_date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (an RFC 3339 timestamp is read as the date written in it, with the time and offset dropped; anything else is refused)

vendor.description: CISA vendorProject, an exact case-insensitive match, e.g. 'Microsoft'

name: kev_recent

catalog_count.description: CISA's own count, in the catalog last fetched.

has_more.description: Whether next_cursor names a further page.

kev_listed_total.description: Every CVE EchelonGraph holds as KEV-listed.

coverage.description: What the answer covers; null where the answer says nothing about it.

kev.description: Newest kev_added_date first; rows within one date are ordered by cve_id.

our_first_seen_kev.description: When EchelonGraph's poller first recorded the CVE entering the catalog; null where no such record exists.

data_truncated.description: false: data is the answer whole. true: the structured result would pass 30,000 characters of JSON with data whole, so data is cut (DATA CUT): the entries of some of its lists keep only some of their fields, or the lists only some of their entries, truncated gives each, and no string is shortened. The same call with full: true returns data whole.

last_successful_fetch_at.description: When CISA last answered our poll of its feed: a 200 we applied, or a 304 Not Modified.

freshness.description: The producing radar's last completed check (last_run_at), where the API serves one.

measured_at.description: When the underlying observation was made, as the API states it; null when the answer does not say or holds no observation.

state.description: measured: a measurement of what was asked; an exposure count is measured only with measured_at and method. not_assessed: the answer holds no dated measurement of what was asked, so no count in it is presented as one; it can still relay a count, as what the source holds on record, undated, and its notes (and exposure_state, where the result carries it) say what each count is.

truncated.description: Present when data_truncated is true: each list of data that was cut, by its path in data (a dot between the names of an object and a list inside it), with total, its entries in the answer, returned, the entries data holds, and thinned, true when each of them keeps only some of its fields.

catalog_count.description: CISA's own count, in the catalog last fetched.

has_more.description: Whether next_cursor names a further page.

kev_listed_total.description: Every CVE EchelonGraph holds as KEV-listed.

kind.description: What failed: the request (network, timeout), the answer (http, not_json, not_object, unexpected_shape), the input, or this server.

message.description: The cause: the API's own message, or what went wrong.

path.description: The API path requested, when a request was made.

status.description: The HTTP status, when the API answered one.

state.description: failed: the lookup did not complete. invalid_input: the input was refused, so nothing was looked up. Neither is a finding.

title: Recent CISA KEV additions
